title: GitHub CLI logins
whyItMatters: The GitHub CLI keeps an OAuth token for every signed-in GitHub account in this folder. With that token a stranger can act as the person on GitHub, including reading private repositories.
source: GitHub CLI manual, environment: config defaults to %AppData%/GitHub CLI on Windows - https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_help_environment
notes: hosts.yml holds the per-host user and oauth_token; config.yml holds preferences. GH_CONFIG_DIR can move the folder. On newer versions the token can be in the Windows credential store instead, so check both.

cleanup.signOut: Revoke the GitHub CLI authorization in the GitHub account Settings under Applications, so the token stored on this PC stops working.
steps: Revoke the GitHub CLI token in the GitHub account Settings under Applications.
Delete the folder named in the plan if it is still there.
Check the account's authorized applications again for anything you do not recognise.
cleanup.risk: Removes the saved GitHub CLI logins on this PC. A token that is not revoked at GitHub keeps working until it expires.
cleanup.source: GitHub CLI manual, gh auth logout: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth_logout
